# Gravity and energy {#sec-ch06}

Gravity does work on the flow, and a finite-volume code has to decide where to book it. At the pin snapy books it
in one way: the face form, which writes the work as a flux difference of potential energy across each cell's $x_1$[^rg-2dff075d305e]
faces (@sec-ch06-face), together with the corrected-PE[^rg-8013ae26823c] face work, which makes the booked work
fourth-order consistent with the scheme's own mass fluxes and is on whenever the grid has a form for it
(@sec-ch06-dwork). The vertical implicit correction carries the same work in its energy row (@sec-ch06-vic), and
@sec-ch06-conserves says which invariant this keeps and which diagnostic measures it. The cell form, which applied
the work $\rho v_1g_1$ in the cell, and the global gravity-work fixer that repaired its budget are not in V3: setup
refuses both, and their sections (@sec-ch06-cell, @sec-ch06-fixer) say only that and why. The momentum equation is the
same in every case; only the energy row is at stake. The hydrostatic reference state these forms are used with is
@sec-ch05; the column solve itself, its assembly, sweep, rejection and stage weighting, is in the time-integration
chapter (@sec-ch09-vic-assembly, @sec-ch09-vic-sweep, @sec-ch09-vic-reject, @sec-ch09-vic-stage), and the device $\Delta t$[^rg-88e66c6f06bb] the
solve reads is derived once, in the execution chapter's section on graph-safe code and the device $\Delta t$
(section 11.5 of the outline, not yet written in the book).

**One identity behind every form.** Every form in this chapter is one identity with a different choice of
discrete potential energy, so it is derived once, here, before the forms that use it.

**The continuous budget.** With constant gravity $g_1$[^rg-4c6f002e02f8] along $x_1$, mass and total energy obey the continuity
equation and the total-energy equation in their usual form,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\partial_t\rho + \nabla\cdot(\rho\mathbf v) &= 0, \\
\partial_tE + \nabla\cdot\big[(E+p)\mathbf v\big] &= \rho v_1g_1 ,
\end{aligned}
$$

with $E$[^rg-da7a263902cd] the total energy density [J m$^{-3}$]. The $x_2$, $x_3$ components of gravity book cell work only and play
no part here. The potential $\phi(x_1) = -g_1x_1$ [m$^2$ s$^{-2}$] does not depend on time, and
$\rho v_1g_1 = -\rho\mathbf v\cdot\nabla\phi$, so $E+\rho\phi$ is conserved:

$$
\partial_t(E+\rho\phi) + \nabla\cdot\big[(E+p+\rho\phi)\mathbf v\big] = 0 .
$$

In a closed domain $\int(E+\rho\phi)\,\mathrm{d}V$ is constant. In this chapter "energy" alone means the total
energy density $E$ of a cell. The conservation diagnostics use the integrated total energy
$E_{\mathrm{tot}} = \sum_iV_iE_i$ [J, per unit horizontal area on Cartesian grids and per steradian on
spherical-polar and cubed-sphere grids], and an invariant written $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$ or
$E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$ is that sum plus a discrete potential energy $P$[^rg-cc5c068f7301] of the same units.

**The exact work in one cell.** Integrate the gravity source over cell $i$[^rg-261e505c3fe9] and write the $x_1$ mass flux density as
$F=\rho v_1$ [kg m$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$]: $\int_{V_i}\rho v_1g_1\,\mathrm{d}V = g_1V_i\langle F\rangle_{V_i}$. Multiply the
continuity equation by $\phi$[^rg-e45e827c3f36] and integrate over the cell, using
$\phi\,\nabla\cdot(\rho\mathbf v) = \nabla\cdot(\phi\rho\mathbf v) - \rho\mathbf v\cdot\nabla\phi$ and the divergence
theorem. Only the $x_1$ faces matter: on Cartesian, spherical-polar and gnomonic-equiangle grids the $x_2$, $x_3$
faces join cells of the same $x_1$ level (on the cubed sphere, the same radius:
{{< code docs/derivations/curved-gravity-work-weight.md >}} §12.6), so their terms
are mass fluxes times one value of $\phi$, which @sec-ch06-dwork treats with the horizontal directions. Rearranged,
the exact gravity work in a cell is

$$
\begin{aligned}
g_1V_i\langle F\rangle_{V_i} &= -\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\mathcal P_i - \Delta_i[A\phi F], \\
\mathcal P_i &= \int_{V_i}\rho\phi\,\mathrm{d}V ,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch06-dwork-template}

with $\Delta_i[\cdot]$ the difference of a face quantity across cell $i$ and $A$ the $x_1$ face area.

**The booked work.** Pick any discrete potential energy $P=\sum_iP_i$ and *define* the booked work by

$$
W_iV_i := -\dot P_i - \Delta_i[A\phi F],
$$ {#eq-ch06-dwork-booked}

with $\dot P_i$ evaluated on the discrete density tendency and $W$ in W m$^{-3}$. Two properties follow.
**Conservation:** summing @eq-ch06-dwork-booked over a column, the $\Delta_i$ terms telescope to the two walls,
where $F=0$, so $\sum_iW_iV_i + \dot P = 0$; the other energy fluxes telescope too, so $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$ is conserved exactly,
whatever $P$ is. **Accuracy:** subtracting @eq-ch06-dwork-booked from @eq-ch06-dwork-template gives
$W_iV_i - g_1V_i\langle F\rangle_{V_i} = \tfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(\mathcal P_i - P_i)$, so the booked work is
exactly as accurate as $P_i$ is as an approximation of the cell's potential energy.

The forms differ only in $P$. The face form takes the piecewise-constant $P=\mathrm{PE}_d$ (@sec-ch06-face); the
corrected-PE face work takes a fourth-order $P$ (@sec-ch06-dwork); the removed cell form had no $P$ at all, which is
why it left a defect (@sec-ch06-cell). The implicit solver carries the same work in its energy row (@sec-ch06-vic),
and @sec-ch06-conserves collects which invariant is kept.

<!-- reader glossary notes -->
[^rg-2dff075d305e]: $x_1, x_2, x_3$ — the three coordinate directions; $x_1$ is always the vertical (radial) direction

[^rg-8013ae26823c]: PE — potential energy

[^rg-88e66c6f06bb]: $\Delta t$ — the step

[^rg-4c6f002e02f8]: $g_1, g_2, g_3$ — constant gravity components [m s$^{-2}$]; $g_1<0$ points to decreasing $x_1$

[^rg-da7a263902cd]: $E$ — total energy density, internal plus kinetic, $\rho e + \tfrac12\rho\lvert\mathbf v\rvert^2$ [J m$^{-3}$]; excludes potential energy

[^rg-cc5c068f7301]: $P$ — corrected discrete potential energy $\sum_iV_i[\rho_i\phi_i - g_1\sigma_i^2s_i[\rho]]$, exact to $O(h^4)$

[^rg-261e505c3fe9]: $i, j, k$ — cell indices in $x_1, x_2, x_3$

[^rg-e45e827c3f36]: $\phi$ — gravitational potential, $\phi(x_1) = -g_1x_1$ (increases upward); never an angle

[^rg-0a78bcb32f8c]: VIC — vertically implicit correction

[^rg-5f155960c1f4]: implicit-scheme — implicit time-integration scheme selector

[^rg-7133da810a58]: gravity-work-fixer — removed in V3: only `false` (the default) is accepted
<!-- end reader glossary notes -->
